problems.title: A range that must stay unchanged
problems.question: The data 4,−3,−5,a,7 have range 12. What must be true about a?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Range = maximum − minimum.
steps: The known minimum −5 and maximum 7 already give range 12. Any a outside [−5,7] would enlarge the range. Every a inside preserves it.

problems.title: Standard deviation of three numbers
problems.question: Find the standard deviation of 1,2,3.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Population standard deviation $\sigma=\sqrt{\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2/n}$.
steps: The mean is 2. Squared deviations total 1+0+1=2; divide by 3 and take the square root.
problems.note: The quiz uses the population standard deviation of the listed data. The sample estimate with denominator n−1 would be 1.

problems.title: A selected volume among three books
problems.question: Choose three uniformly from six book volumes. Find the probability that volume 4 is included.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: $P=\binom52/\binom63$.
steps: Choose two more volumes from the other five: 10 favourable selections out of 20. The probability is 1/2.

problems.title: Cone sector angle and inclination
problems.question: The developed lateral sector of a cone has central angle 210°. Find the cosine of the angle between a generator and the base plane.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: $2\pi r=(210/360)2\pi l$; $\cos\theta=r/l$.
steps: The sector arc becomes the base circumference, so $r/l=210/360=7/12$. The generator projects to a base radius, giving the same ratio for cos theta.
problems.note: The listed 1/2, 7/9, 5/6 and 1/5 do not contain the correct value 7/12.

problems.title: An off-axis cylindrical section
problems.question: A cylinder of radius 5 has an axis-parallel section distance 4 from the axis, with area 80. Find its generator length.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Chord length $=2\sqrt{R^2-d^2}$; section area = chord length × cylinder height.
steps: The chord is $2\sqrt{25-16}=6$. Hence the height is 80/6=40/3, also the generator length.

problems.title: Four-digit multiples of four
problems.question: How many four-digit multiples of 4 use digits 1,2,3,4 exactly once?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Divisibility by 4 depends on the final two digits.
steps: The valid two-digit endings with distinct allowed digits are 12,24,32. For each ending, the two unused digits can be arranged in 2 ways.
Total: 3×2=6.

problems.title: Four white balls without replacement
problems.question: A box has 5 white and 7 black balls. Choose 4 randomly. Find the probability all are white.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: $P=\binom54/\binom{12}4$.
steps: There are 5 favourable selections and 495 total selections, giving 5/495=1/99.

problems.title: Triangles from circle points
problems.question: Eight distinct points lie on a circle. How many triangles have vertices among them?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Each choice of three points gives one nondegenerate triangle: $\binom83$.
steps: A straight line meets a circle at at most two distinct points, so no triple is collinear. The count is 8×7×6/6=56.

problems.title: An equation with no real solution
problems.question: Which listed equation has empty solution set?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
steps: $|-3x|+3\ge3$, so it cannot equal zero. The other equations have real roots: $x=-3\pm\sqrt3$, $x=-1/9$, and x=−1 respectively.

problems.title: A sphere fitting inside a cylinder
problems.question: A sphere is contained in a cylinder, without necessarily being inscribed. Which listed cylinder-to-sphere volume ratio is possible: 1.2,1.3,1.4,1.7?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: For sphere radius r, cylinder radius R≥r and height h≥2r; ratio $=\pi R^2h/(4\pi r^3/3)\ge3/2$.
steps: Only 1.7 is at least 1.5. It is realizable, for example take R=r and h=34r/15, giving ratio 1.7.

problems.title: Distinct digits between three hundred and eight hundred
problems.question: Count integers from 300 through 800 inclusive with all three digits distinct.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Multiplication rule: choose hundreds, then tens, then units.
steps: For hundreds digit 3,4,5,6,7 there are 5 choices. Tens can be any of the other 9 digits, including zero; units any of the remaining 8.
Total 5×9×8=360. The endpoint 800 has repeated zeroes and adds nothing.

problems.title: Opposite exponents cannot agree
problems.question: How many real solutions satisfy $(0.25)^x=4^{1/x}$?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: x≠0 and $0.25=4^{-1}$; equal positive-base powers have equal exponents.
steps: The equation requires −x=1/x, or x²=−1. This has no real roots.

problems.title: Distance from the origin to a line
problems.question: Find distance from (0,0) to x+2y=4.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
steps: The line is x+2y−4=0. Thus d=4/√(1+4)=4/√5.

problems.title: Volume of a regular triangular pyramid
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has base side 3 cm and height 4 cm. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Equilateral base area $B=\sqrt3a^2/4$; pyramid volume $V=Bh/3$.
steps: $B=9\sqrt3/4$. Therefore $V=(9\sqrt3/4)4/3=3\sqrt3$ cm³.

problems.title: A smaller pyramid inside a trapezoidal pyramid
problems.question: Pyramid MABCD has trapezoidal base with BC=2,AD=3 and volume 10. K is midpoint of MC. Find volume KBCD.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Volume ratio = base-area ratio × height ratio.
steps: Triangle BCD and the trapezoid have the same planar altitude, so their area ratio is BC/(BC+AD)=2/5.
K has half M’s height above the base. The volume is $10\cdot(2/5)\cdot(1/2)=2$.

problems.title: Three vessels share a tank
problems.question: Of a tank’s water, 2/5 goes to the first vessel, 1/2 to the second, and the third gets 6 litres less than the first. Find the initial total.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: The remaining fraction is $1-2/5-1/2=1/10$.
steps: For total T, the condition is T/10=2T/5−6. Thus 3T/10=6 and T=20 litres.

problems.title: Fourth powers of sine and cosine
problems.question: If sin2x=1/3, find $\sin^4x+\cos^4x$.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: $\sin^4x+\cos^4x=1-2\sin^2x\cos^2x=1-\tfrac12\sin^22x$.
steps: Substitute sin²2x=1/9 to get 1−1/18=17/18.

problems.title: A midpoint parallel section of a pyramid
problems.question: A plane through the midpoint of the pyramid height is parallel to its base. The base area is 24. Find section area.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Linear similarity ratio 1/2 gives area ratio 1/4.
steps: The smaller pyramid above the section has half the original height. Therefore the section area is 24/4=6.

problems.title: A vector identity in a divided triangle
problems.question: M is on AB, N on BC with BM:MA=BN:NC=1:2. Express vector MC in terms of MN and MA.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Choose B as origin, $A=3u,C=3v,M=u,N=v$.
steps: $MC=3v-u$, $MN=v-u$, $MA=2u$. Thus $3MN+MA=3v-3u+2u=3v-u=MC$.

problems.title: Quadrant of a parabola vertex
problems.question: In which quadrant is the vertex of $y=(2021x+12)^2-\sqrt{199}$?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: The square is minimized when its inner expression is zero.
steps: The vertex is $(-12/2021,-\sqrt{199})$. Both coordinates are negative, so it is in quadrant III.

problems.title: Four-digit numbers with each of two digits repeated twice
problems.question: Count four-digit numbers using exactly two different digits, each appearing twice.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: For two distinct nonzero digits there are $4!/(2!2!)=6$ arrangements.
steps: Choose two from digits 1–9: 36 pairs, giving 216 numbers.
For a pair consisting of zero and one of 9 nonzero digits, choose the other location of the nonzero digit after fixing the first digit nonzero: 3 arrangements per pair.
The total is 216+27=243.

problems.title: A union probability with missing joint information
problems.question: Events A,B have P(A)=0.95 and P(B)=0.6. Find P(A union B).
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$; intersection bounds are $0.55\le P(A\cap B)\le0.6$.
steps: The given marginals yield only $0.95\le P(A\cup B)\le1$. Without an intersection probability or independence assumption, the union is not uniquely determined.
The listed 0.97,0.98,0.99 are all possible, from intersections 0.58,0.57,0.56 respectively. The listed 0.92 is impossible.
If independence is added, the intersection is 0.95×0.6=0.57 and the union is 0.98.
problems.answer: Underdetermined: any value in [0.95,1]; under independence, 0.98.
problems.note: The source does not state independence. Three of its choices are compatible with the given probabilities, so a unique choice is unjustified.

problems.title: A subtriangle angle
problems.question: K lies on AC, angles BAC=BCA=30°, and BKC=80°. Find KBC.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Triangle angle sum is 180°.
steps: In triangle BKC, angle BCK is 30° because CK points along CA. Thus KBC=180−80−30=70°.

problems.title: Percentage decrease of a right-triangle area
problems.question: One leg increases by 10% and the other decreases by 40%. By what percentage does the area decrease?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Area $=ab/2$, so its multiplier is the product of leg multipliers.
steps: The new area is 1.1×0.6=0.66 of the old area. The decrease is 1−0.66=0.34, or 34%.

problems.title: Compare a logarithm, a combination and a factorial
problems.question: Order $a=\log_3199,b=\binom52,c=3!$.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
steps: Thus 4<a<5, while c=6 and b=10. Therefore a<c<b.

problems.title: Who makes up the dismissed group?
problems.question: 80% of staff were diligent. 90% of diligent staff stay; 85% of lazy staff are dismissed. What percentage of the dismissed staff were diligent?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Conditional share = dismissed diligent / total dismissed.
steps: For 100 staff, 80 are diligent and 20 lazy. Dismissed diligent: 8; dismissed lazy: 17.
The requested share is 8/(8+17)=8/25=32%.

problems.title: Area of a right trapezoid
problems.question: The base sum is 20, the leg sum 18, and acute angle 30°. Find the area.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: If the oblique leg is l, height $h=l\sin30^\circ=l/2$; area $=(a+b)h/2$.
steps: The legs are h and 2h, so 3h=18 and h=6. The area is 20×6/2=60.

problems.title: Rhombus area from one diagonal
problems.question: A rhombus has side 5 cm and diagonal 8 cm. Find its area.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Half diagonals are perpendicular, so $5^2=4^2+(d/2)^2$; area $=8d/2$.
steps: The other half-diagonal is 3, so d=6. The area is 8×6/2=24 cm².

problems.title: An exponential inequality
problems.question: Solve $3^{x+2}>3^x+2$.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: $3^{x+2}=9\cdot3^x$ and the base-3 exponential is increasing.
steps: The inequality becomes $8\cdot3^x>2$, or $3^x>1/4$. Taking base-3 logarithms gives $x>\log_3(1/4)$.

problems.title: A tilted square section through two base chords
problems.question: A cylinder has radius and height 4 cm. Parallel chords AB and CD in its upper and lower bases form square ABCD, whose plane is not axis-parallel. Find AB.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Equal parallel chords have equal absolute offsets d from the axis. Chord square $a^2=4(R^2-d^2)$.
steps: The offsets must be on opposite sides; equal same-side offsets would give an axis-parallel plane. Thus corresponding endpoints differ horizontally by 2d and vertically by 4.
The square side also has $a^2=16+4d^2$. Equating with $64-4d^2$ gives d²=6 and a²=40.

problems.title: Rotate an isosceles triangle about an equal side
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has side ratio 5:5:6. Rotating about an equal-side line produces surface area 10π. Find its triangle area.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: For sides 5t,5t,6t, area $S=12t^2$; distance to the rotation axis $r=2S/(5t)=24t/5$. Cone lateral area is $\pi rl$.
steps: The perpendicular foot lies inside the length-5t axis side: its distance from one endpoint is 7t/5. Thus the outer surface consists of two cones with slant lengths 5t and 6t.
The surface is $\pi(24t/5)(11t)=264\pi t^2/5=10\pi$. Hence t²=25/132.
The original triangle area is $12(25/132)=25/11$.

problems.title: A system involving cubes
problems.question: Solve x+y=3 and x³+y³=9.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
steps: 9=27−9xy gives xy=2. Thus x and y are the roots of t²−3t+2=0, namely 1 and 2.
Both orders satisfy the system.

problems.title: A forgotten notebook adds a return trip
problems.question: Anna normally walks to school in 20 minutes. At one point she could continue and arrive 3 minutes early, or return home then go to school and arrive 7 minutes late. What fraction had she walked?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: The alternative adds twice the home-to-current-point travel time.
steps: The arrival difference is 3+7=10 minutes. Thus twice the elapsed walking time is 10, giving elapsed time 5 minutes.
At constant speed, the distance fraction equals time fraction 5/20=1/4.

problems.title: An inscribed square with half the area
problems.question: M,N,K,T lie on consecutive sides AB,BC,CD,DA of square ABCD, and MNKT is a square. A uniformly random point of ABCD lies inside MNKT with probability 0.5. Find MB:BN.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: For outer side s, put MB=u and BN=v; square geometry gives u+v=s. Inner side squared is u²+v².
steps: The area ratio is $(u^2+v^2)/(u+v)^2=1/2$. Multiplying out gives $2u^2+2v^2=u^2+2uv+v^2$.
Thus (u−v)²=0 and u=v. This is the midpoint square, which indeed has half the outer area.

problems.title: Shared intercept and an integer minimum
problems.question: Natural a,b give lines y=ax+5 and y=3x+b the same x-axis intercept. Minimize a²+b.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate count, identity or geometric equation and check the result against the printed choices.
formulas: Equal intercepts give $-5/a=-b/3$, hence ab=15.
steps: Positive factor pairs (a,b) are (1,15),(3,5),(5,3),(15,1). Their objective values are 16,14,28,226.
The minimum is 14, attained at a=3,b=5. The two lines may coincide; the source does not require distinct lines.
